All of these agents are indicated for Tinea Corporis, a fungal infection of the skin. The scores for these relationships are consistent, indicating a plausible but not definitive link. The mechanism of action for these antifungal agents is not fully elucidated, but their shared indication for Tinea Corporis suggests a possible overlap in their therapeutic targets. The evidence supports a potential repurposing of Betamethasone for Tinea Corporis, though further research is needed to confirm the clinical relevance and underlying biological pathways.
